name: Lady Jane
description: Lady Jane is a complex two-deck solitaire game belonging to the Spider family. It is characterized by its large tableau of 10 piles and the requirement to build up eight foundations in suit. On the tableau, build down alternating colors; only same-suit sequences can be moved as a unit, requiring tactical planning to keep suits together. Stock deals 3 cards at a time to waste; one redeal allowed.

history.origins: Part of the late 20th-century expansion of computer-based solitaire games. It evolved as a hybrid between the foundation-building of Klondike and the large-move mechanics of Spider.
timeline: 1980s: Two-deck solitaire variations flourish in digital formats.
1990s: Lady Jane is standardized in large digital solitaire suites (e.g., SolSuite).
Present: A popular choice for players who find Spider too difficult but Klondike too simple.
history.cultural: Often categorized as a 'Relaxation Solitaire' due to the high volume of possible moves in the mid-game.
history.evolution: The game was designed to have a higher win-rate than traditional Spider by allowing cross-suit building on the tableau.

setup.players: One player only. Lady Jane is a solitaire (patience) game; the player manages the entire layout—ten tableau piles, eight foundations, stock, and waste—making all moves alone.
setup.dealing: Deal 10 tableau piles: first pile 1 card, second 2, third 3, and so on up to 10 (55 cards total). Place the remaining 49 cards face down as stock. Eight foundation piles and waste start empty.
setup.equipment: Table space for 10 tableau piles, 8 foundation piles, stock and waste.

rules.objective: Move all 104 cards to the eight foundation piles, building up in suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Foundations**: Build up in suit from Ace to King. Cards are moved individually.
2. **Tableau**: Build down alternating colors. Cards may be moved individually or as a group if built down in suit. An empty tableau pile may be filled by any exposed card or in-suit sequence from another tableau.
3. **Stock**: Tap the stock to turn up 3 cards at a time to the waste pile. Only one redeal is allowed.
4. **Waste**: The top card is available for play onto the tableau or foundations.
keyRules: Foundations: build up in suit from Ace to King; cards moved individually.
Tableau: build down alternating colors; in-suit sequences may move as a unit; empty pile accepts any card or valid sequence.
Stock: tap to turn 3 cards to waste; only one redeal allowed.
Waste: top card is available for play to tableau or foundations.

strategy.basic: Prioritize suit matching on the tableau even though it's not required. If you don't keep Spades on Spades, you will quickly find yourself with 10 'blocked' piles that cannot be moved as units.
strategy.intermediate: Empty Space Utility: Create an empty tableau pile as quickly as possible. This acts as a 'staging area' for breaking up cross-suit stacks and reorganizing them into in-suit sequences.
strategy.advanced: Foundation Stalling: Don't move a card to the foundations if it can be used on the tableau to build an in-suit sequence. For example, if you have a 4 of Hearts on the tableau and a 5 of Hearts in the waste, don't put it in the foundation yetâ€”use it to free up a Hearts sequence on the tableau.
tips: The large 10th pile is your biggest challenge. Dig into it early to reveal the cards buried at the bottom.
Always check the foundations before dealing from the stockâ€”missing a 2 that could have cleared a big tableau stack is a common game-losing mistake.
